Comparable phosphorus periods

The three permits mapped upstream of USGS-02186702 are Upper Eighteenmile, Middle Eighteenmile and Milliken. These summaries retain the same EPA reporting feature for each permit.

Full years · 2024 → 2025

520.70 → 955.70 kg

83.54% change in the sum of twelve reported monthly phosphorus loads at each of the three permits.

Same months · January–August 2025 → 2026

655.73 → 948.33 kg

44.62% change across the same eight numeric monthly periods at all three permits. Milliken contributes 791.95 kg to the 2026 subtotal.

The 2025 total is close to 2023 (949.71 kg). Across the same supported three-permit cohort in 2021–2025, yearly totals range from 520.70 to 985.58 kg; 2024 is the low year in that interval.

The gauge relationship comes from current retained DES/NHD routing. Historical reporting-feature identities remain distinct. Pendleton–Clemson is mapped downstream and has its own comparison rows.

Original series and comparison records

How the records are compared

Original identity. Each series retains permit, EPA reporting feature, monitoring location and parameter code. Total nitrogen, ammonia and nitrate stay separate. Milliken features 001, T1M and T1Q keep their original identities across the source history.

Available period sum. The sum uses numeric EPA published monitoring-period loads whose periods had ended at capture. A historical full-year comparison requires twelve unique numeric single-month periods, each with its exact calendar month start and end. Duplicate months, nonmonthly intervals, nonnumeric records and partial years stay visible in coverage and original-source inspection. The year index follows the original period-ending year; this explorer does not prorate cross-year quarterly records.

Current-year comparison. The 2026 comparison uses the intersection of unique numeric calendar months in 2025 and 2026 for each original series. The three-permit comparison further intersects those months across all three members. These are reported-period subtotals for the displayed months. Future source placeholders are retained in the original-period view and excluded from subtotals.

Published annual selectors. The source contains both p_est=N and p_est=Y requests. All 303 selected series-year rows with one numeric annual value under both selectors returned equal displayed values. The raw estimation factors, original annual arrays and differences from available period sums are retained. For example, 2026 Milliken T1M phosphorus is 1,189 kg in both published annual selectors and 791.95 kg across its available January–August periods. Published annual values and period sums remain distinct measures.

Non-detect handling. The original EPA load requests use p_nd=ZERO. Numeric values are retained as published under that setting; original non-detect flags and NODI descriptions remain attached. A nonnumeric original value stays missing. Blank table cells use an em dash, including percentage changes with a zero or unsupported denominator.

Scientific use. These rows describe reported point-source discharges. Current gauge routing supplies contextual group labels; original historical coordinates remain in the retained source. The existing 2023 calendar-weighted discharge calculation and watershed model outputs retain their own physical and temporal bases. The 2023 three-permit phosphorus period sum here is 949.71 kg; the separate calendar-weighted science result remains 949.31580872 kg.

Retained input identities and original source access

Every inspected annual or comparison row carries original response IDs and JSON pointers. Source links open the corresponding original public EPA request. The embedded source catalog records the captured response hashes; live responses may advance after capture.
